description: Since the 1960s, NASA has left hardware across the Moon, Mars, and deep space—monuments to human curiosity that completed their missions and paved the way for future exploration. CosmicRelics is an interactive digital museum and storytelling application designed to introduce school-age space enthusiasts to the hardware left behind and the groundbreaking science it made possible.
summary:
Since the 1960s, NASA has left hardware across the Moon, Mars, and deep space—monuments to human curiosity that completed their missions and paved the way for future exploration. CosmicRelics is an interactive digital museum and storytelling application designed to introduce school-age space enthusiasts to the hardware left behind and the groundbreaking science it made possible.

Through an illustrated, planetarium-style interface, students explore six iconic artifacts: the Apollo 11 Lunar Module "Eagle" descent stage, Opportunity Mars rover ("Oppy"), Surveyor 3, InSight Mars geophysics lander, the Apollo 17 Lunar Roving Vehicle, and Voyager 1 carrying the Golden Record. CosmicRelics explains the rocket equation physics behind why hardware is left behind, details each artifact's current resting state, simulates archival CAPCOM audio transmissions, and provides youth-friendly "Did You Know?" facts. An interactive "Junior Relic Curator Quiz" allows young explorers to test their knowledge and earn a certified digital space curator badge.
details:
1. WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

CosmicRelics serves as an educational museum console highlighting discarded off-world hardware:

• Celestial Body Filter: Filter exhibits across the Moon, Mars, and Interstellar Deep Space.

• 6 Featured Relic Exhibits:

1. Apollo 11 "Eagle" Descent Stage: Explains how leaving landing legs saved liftoff fuel, while highlighting the Laser Ranging Retroreflector still pinged by Earth lasers today.

2. Opportunity Rover: Chronicles Oppy's 14-year, 45-km marathon, the discovery of hematite blueberries, and its final transmission during the 2018 global dust storm.

3. Surveyor 3 Lander: Explains how Apollo 12 astronauts retrieved its camera to test space weathering.

4. InSight Mars Lander: Details how its SEIS seismometer recorded 1,300 marsquakes before red dust coated its solar wings.

5. Apollo 17 Lunar Rover (LRV): Details Gene Cernan's taped map fender and how it was parked to broadcast the lunar liftoff.

6. Voyager 1 & The Golden Record: Covers the time capsule carrying Earth's sounds into interstellar space.

• Interactive Planetary Radar Canvas: Animated canvas rendering latitude/longitude coordinates and beacon pulses on lunar and Martian globes.

• Archival Audio Simulator: Uses the Web Audio API to simulate retro CAPCOM radio chirps.

• Junior Curator Quiz: Interactive 3-question challenge awarding a certified digital curator credential.

2. BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

Inspires elementary and middle school students to explore aerospace engineering and history. Demystifies why hardware is left behind (the rocket equation and payload mass budgets) and highlights historical preservation on other worlds.

3. TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED

HTML5 Canvas, CSS3 responsive dark-mode styling, vanilla JavaScript, and Web Audio API synthesis. Completely self-contained with zero external dependencies.

4. CREATIVITY & INNOVATION

Transforms dry coordinate catalogs into an engaging, story-driven exhibit combining planetary radar coordinates with historical storytelling and radio audio effects.

5. FACTORS CONSIDERED

Addressed planetary protection ethics, vacuum vs atmospheric weathering differences, and the operational transition from robotic precursors to crewed Artemis landings.
